papers.title: Thermal conductivity tuning of scalable nanopatterned silicon membranes measured with a three-probe method
papers.abstract: Phononic silicon structures have emerged as an integrable and scalable nanosystem for tailoring thermal transport. However, their widespread adoption has been limited by their complex fabrication pathways. Alongside, the reliable characterization of thermal properties in suspended nanostructured films remains challenging, as thermal contact resistances often hinder the accuracy of measurements.   In this work, we demonstrate a clear and controllable reduction of thermal conductivity in nanopatterned silicon membranes. A block copolymer self-assembly approach is employed to fabricate nanoholed silicon films with a pitch of 63 nm and hole diameters of 35 nm. Additionally, we introduce an extension of the three-probe technique that enables robust, quantitative, and spatially resolved thermal conductivity measurements in complex thin-film systems, accounting for thermal contact artifacts.   The method is validated through measurements on unpatterned 40 nm-thick silicon thin films between 30 and 350 K, yielding a room-temperature thermal conductivity of 46.5 W/m.K. Finally, we further show that controlled etching of the nanoholes provides a powerful means to tune thermal transport in the overall studied temperature range, establishing hole etch depth control as an effective parameter in phononic silicon. Specifically, a fivefold reduction in thermal conductivity is achieved, reaching 7.3 W/m.K for fully etched-through membranes at room temperature.

summary_zh.motivation: 实现可集成纳米图案化硅膜的热导率调控与精确测量。
summary_zh.method: 使用嵌段共聚物自组装制备纳米孔硅膜，并扩展三探针技术测量热导率。
summary_zh.result: 获得室温热导率46.5 W/m.K，完全刻蚀后降低至7.3 W/m.K。
summary_zh.validation: 通过未图案化硅薄膜的宽温区测量验证方法准确性。

summary_en.motivation: To achieve controllable thermal conductivity reduction and reliable measurement in scalable nanopatterned silicon membranes.
summary_en.method: Nanoholed silicon films were fabricated via block copolymer self-assembly, and a three-probe technique was extended for quantitative thermal conductivity measurements accounting for contact resistances.
summary_en.result: A room-temperature thermal conductivity of 46.5 W/m.K was measured for unpatterned films, and a fivefold reduction to 7.3 W/m.K was achieved in fully etched-through membranes.
summary_en.validation: The method was validated by measuring unpatterned silicon thin films from 30 to 350 K, showing good agreement with known values.

papers.title: Migration patterns of uncemented femoral stems in hip replacement: a systematic review and meta-analysis of clinical radiostereometric analysis cohort studies
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of radiostereometric analysis studies of primary uncemented femoral stems to investigate their subsidence and retroversion patterns and the migration patterns according to implant, patient, and study characteristics. METHODS: A systematic search of PubMed, Web of Science, Cochrane, and Embase databases to identify all radiostereometric analysis studies on femoral stem migration following primary uncemented total hip replacement was performed. Clinical studies with 2 or more postoperative radiostereometric measurements within 2 years were included. Subsidence and retroversion at 6 weeks, 3 and 6 months, 1, 2, 5, and 10 years were included for analysis. Extracted implant characteristics included implant design, coating, and surgical approach. Data was analyzed using a random effects model. RESULTS: 73 studies on 120 cohorts and 2,970 uncemented stems were included. 119 cohorts reported on subsidence and 91 on retroversion. The pooled subsidence at 3 months was 0.29 mm (95% confidence interval [CI] 0.19-0.39) and 0.32 mm (CI 0.21-0.43) at 2 years. The pooled retroversion at 3 months was 0.51° (CI 0.33-0.70) and 0.70° (CI 0.48-0.93) at 2 years. Hydroxyapatite-coated stems showed the least migration (subsidence 0.26 mm; CI 0.13-0.40; retroversion 0.51°; CI 0.22-0.80) among different coating types. The anterior approach showed more migration (subsidence 1.04 mm, CI 0.53-1.55; retroversion 1.52°, CI 1.08-1.95) than other surgical approaches. CONCLUSION: Our study shows that most subsidence and retroversion of uncemented femoral stems occurs during the first 3 months. Stabilization of subsidence occurred after 3 months, and retroversion stabilized after 2 years. Migration patterns differ based on stem type, coating, surgical approach, the time period when inclusion started, and timing of baseline measurement.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文提供了股骨柄临床迁移模式的荟萃数据，但对于用户研究的AI生物打印、髋关节植入物力学仿真或增材制造方向无直接指导作用。
llm.why_not_core: This paper is a clinical meta-analysis of radiostereometric migration data; it does not involve finite element analysis, additive manufacturing, artificial intelligence, or implant design optimization.

summary_zh.motivation: 系统综述未涂层股骨柄的临床迁移模式。
summary_zh.method: 对73项RSA研究进行荟萃分析，提取下沉和旋转数据。
summary_zh.result: 大部分下沉发生在3个月内，羟基磷灰石涂层柄迁移最少。
summary_zh.validation: 基于临床RSA队列的荟萃分析。

summary_en.motivation: To systematically review and meta-analyze subsidence and retroversion patterns of uncemented femoral stems from clinical radiostereometric analysis studies.
summary_en.method: A meta-analysis of 73 RSA studies (120 cohorts, 2970 stems) was performed using a random effects model to pool migration data at multiple time points.
summary_en.result: Subsidence stabilized after 3 months (pooled 0.32 mm at 2 years) while retroversion continued to increase up to 2 years (0.70°), with hydroxyapatite-coated stems showing the least migration.
summary_en.validation: Clinical validation through meta-analysis of published RSA cohort studies with confidence intervals.
